$comment: Generated by `fathom_analyze::insight::schema_document()`. Do not hand-edit: change the types or the generator and re-run `fathom analyze --schema --write`. Owner: `e2.11` (`reco-tt4`).

episode.description: The episode's identity, carried from the spine so a payload can be relinked after a rewrite without asking the store again.

attribution.description: The attribution behind `author_kind`, with the evidence that produced it (`e4.1`). Absent on a row written before migration 4, which stored the label and nothing else.

agent.description: The agent the evidence named, when it named exactly one.

confidence.description: Confidence in `kind`; 0.0 means nothing was known, not that nothing matters.

evidence.description: Every rung that fired, strongest first.

detail.description: The literal, in the commit's own spelling.

reason.description: Why the verdict is `unknown`, or why a label was refused rather than guessed.

author_kind.description: `agent`, `human` or `unknown` — `unknown` is a value, never a guess.

boundary_rule.description: Which segmentation rule opened this episode (`ADR-003 §4.7`).

fingerprint.description: The strong digest (author, subject, path set).

first_utc.description: First member timestamp in milliseconds since the epoch — the store unit.

id.description: ADR-003 §2.1's derived id — what a review is keyed to.

last_utc.description: Last member timestamp in milliseconds since the epoch.

lineage_ref.description: The lineage the episode sits on.

live.description: Whether a current commit still belongs to it.

members.description: Member commit SHAs, capped; `n_commits` is the truth.

session.description: The harness session, when one was recorded (`ADR-005`).

turn.description: The harness turn, when one was recorded.

evidence.description: Where a figure's proof lives: a JSON pointer inside this document, a command the reviewer can run, or the plan key that owns the missing answer. At least one is always set — `verify` fails a figure that carries none.

owner.description: The plan key that owns the answer, e.g. `e3.2`.

pointer.description: A JSON pointer into this document, e.g. `#/files`.

run.description: A command this binary answers to, e.g. `fathom show HEAD~3`.

figure.description: One printed claim, with the integers behind it and the pointer to its evidence. `value` is what a surface prints verbatim; `raw` is what a machine compares. A figure that was not measured is `known: false` and carries the reason it was not — never a zero.

confidence.description: 0..=1, present only when the figure is an estimate.

known.description: Whether anything was measured. `false` prints as `?`.

label.description: The short label printed before the value.

raw.description: The integers behind `value`, sorted by key.

reason.description: Why it is unknown. Required in substance when `known` is false.

value.description: The value as the product words it. Empty when `known` is false.

file.description: One path the episode touched, with the taxonomy decisions it was classified by. Most figure pointers land here, so the rows carry their own provenance.

basis.description: `full` (per-commit rows) or `rollup` (the summed per-path read a rail page uses).

change.description: What git asserted about the path. `unrecorded` means the read did not look, not that nothing happened.

commits.description: Member commits that touched this path.

old_path.description: The path it came from, when the index asserted a move.

surface.description: The reviewer-facing surface, from the one classifier in `fathom_analyze::risk`.

gap.description: Why a section is not a full answer, who owns the rest, and what to run meanwhile.

owner.description: The plan key that owns the answer.

reason.description: What is missing, stated as a fact about this build.

remedy.description: A command the reviewer can run instead, when one exists.

section.description: The section this gap belongs to.

short.description: The one-line version, for the brief: a card row has room for this and not for `reason`.

integrity.description: The document's own verdict on itself, from `EpisodeDelta::verify`.

checks.description: What was checked, so `verified` has a definition.

problems.description: One line per problem found; empty when `verified`.

provenance.description: Where the rows came from, so a figure can be traced to a read.

epoch.description: The index epoch the rows came from.

files_detail.description: `full` when the per-commit file rows were read, `rollup` when the summed per-path read was used.

risk.description: The ranking, with its arithmetic and its blind spots. Absent means unranked, which is not rank 0.

model.description: Which ranking produced the number (`spine-1` today).

vector.description: `spine-1 88 = surfaces 50 + size 12 + …` — the arithmetic, checkable from the row.

section.description: One of the seven questions. All seven are always present; a section that could not answer is `unavailable` with a gap, never missing.

figures.description: The figures, capped and ordered; the remainder is counted, not cut.

id.description: The section id. The seven below are the contract; a reader must ignore one it does not know rather than fail on it, which is what makes an appended section an additive change.

owner.description: The plan key whose analysis owns a full answer.

remainder.description: How many figures the cap dropped — counted, never silently cut.

sectionState.description: The three claims a reviewer acts on differently.

totals.description: The episode's scale, and what of it a review reads. The derived four are arithmetic, and `verify` re-does it.

discounted_churn.description: Churn discounted as noise: three quarters of the churn on generated, vendored, lockfile, binary and dependency paths.

files_read.description: Grouped file rows the read returned.

files_truncated.description: Whether the read hit its cap.

reconciles.description: Whether the rows seen sum to the episode counts; absent when the cap bound and the question cannot be answered.

description: One episode as one versioned document: identity, rows, derived totals, the seven analysis sections with their evidence, the ranking, the gaps and a self-check. The TUI card, `fathom analyze --json`, the review artefact (`e5.7`) and the MCP tools (`e6.4`) are renderings of this and compute nothing of their own.

files.description: The rows the figures are derived from, in path order.

gaps.description: Every gap in one list, section order — the same objects the sections carry.

sections.description: The seven sections, in contract order. `minItems` is seven because a missing section is a missing question; a newer producer may append one, which is why there is no `maxItems`.

title: Fathom episode delta

x-fathom.compatibility: additive changes keep the version; breaking changes bump it
